fix: Shor's algorithm breaks RSA outright. Replace key transport with ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and signatures with ML-DSA (FIPS 204), or run a hybrid until the peer catches up.

msg: RSA under 2048 bits is already disallowed — this is not a 2030 problem, it is a today problem.
fix: Nothing below RSA-2048 has been acceptable since 2013. Go straight to ML-KEM / ML-DSA rather than re-keying to RSA-2048, which is itself deprecated after 2030-12-31.
Elliptic-curve signatures fall to Shor exactly like RSA, only faster. ML-DSA (FIPS 204) is the drop-in; SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) is the conservative hash-based option for firmware and roots of trust.

Key agreement is the harvest-now-decrypt-later surface: the handshake an attacker records today is decrypted the day a CRQC exists. Wrap it as a hybrid — X25519MLKEM768 — so it is safe under either assumption.
Finite-field DH is in the same Shor class as RSA and ECDH. Replace or hybridise with ML-KEM (FIPS 203).

msg: DSA signature generation is already disallowed — FIPS 186-5 withdrew it, so this fails a FIPS review today, before any quantum argument.
fix: Move to ML-DSA (FIPS 204). Do not detour through ECDSA: it is deprecated after 2030-12-31 anyway.
Ed25519 is a discrete-log signature in the same elliptic-curve family as ECDSA, so Shor breaks it on the same day. NIST IR 8547 withdraws the whole family. Plan ML-DSA (FIPS 204).

what: TLS group list with no hybrid
fix: Add a hybrid group so the handshake survives a later CRQC: X25519MLKEM768 (and P-256 + ML-KEM-768 where a FIPS curve is required). Browsers already negotiate it, so adding it costs nothing at the client end.

what: SSH key exchange with no post-quantum method
fix: OpenSSH already ships post-quantum key exchange: mlkem768x25519-sha256 and sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com. Put one of them first in KexAlgorithms.

msg: ssh-rsa is the SHA-1 RSA signature algorithm — OpenSSH disabled it by default in 8.8 (2021), so this line is already breaking connections, not just aging.
fix: If you must stay on RSA short-term use rsa-sha2-256/512; the durable move is ML-DSA once your server fleet supports it.

msg: SHA-1 in a signature or certificate is disallowed — NIST is retiring SHA-1 entirely by 2030-12-31 and signature use was disallowed long before that.
fix: SHA-256 or SHA-384 today. Note that hash-based signatures such as SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) depend on hash strength, so fixing this is also a prerequisite for the post-quantum path.

msg: Three-key Triple DES has been disallowed for encryption since the end of 2023 — a compliance finding today, independent of quantum.
fix: AES-256-GCM. Use the same change window to size symmetric keys for a post-quantum world.

msg: AES-128 is not broken, but Grover's algorithm reduces its brute-force cost to roughly 2^64 operations and NSA CNSA 2.0 requires AES-256.
fix: AES-256-GCM for anything whose confidentiality has to outlive the record you are keeping it in. Symmetric is the cheap half of this migration — do it first.

msg: MD5 is collision-broken and disallowed for any signature, certificate or integrity purpose.
fix: SHA-256 or SHA-384. If this is a non-security cache key, say so in the code — a reviewer cannot tell the difference from here, and neither can an auditor.

what: JWT/JWS signed with a classical algorithm
fix: Tokens and their verification keys live in clients you do not control, so the verifier fleet is the long pole. Start the ML-DSA (FIPS 204) swap behind a `kid` before the fleet becomes the blocker.

msg: PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption padding is Bleichenbacher-oracle territory and is a finding on its own, before any quantum argument.
fix: OAEP today; ML-KEM (FIPS 203) as the destination. Encapsulation with ML-KEM removes the padding-oracle class entirely.

what: no post-quantum replacement named anywhere in this file
msg: This file leans on quantum-vulnerable public-key crypto and names no post-quantum replacement anywhere — nothing in it is on a migration path.
fix: FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), 204 (ML-DSA) and 205 (SLH-DSA) were published on 2024-08-13. The replacements exist; name the one you intend to use, in this file, next to the algorithm it replaces.
